From PDF to retrieved chunk: testing a RAGFlow ingestion pipeline

Four stages, tested end to end on a 5-page document: MinerU parsing, a custom footnote-linking step, RAGFlow chunking, and RAGFlow embedding and retrieval. Plus what happens to images, and why the pipeline has to be self-hosted.

The problem being tested

A table row says an exclusion applies, and names a footnote. The footnote that says what actually qualifies is printed two pages later. Split that document into chunks the ordinary way and the two halves land in different chunks, so a search can return the row without the condition that governs it.

RAGFlow is an open-source retrieval engine. It reads a document, splits it into chunks, turns each chunk into a vector, and searches those chunks to answer a question. A chunk is the unit that gets retrieved, so whatever is missing from the chunk is missing from the answer.

The document below was written to contain that problem, along with five other things a parser has to survive.

What is being testedWhere it is
Merged cellsTable 1: four full-width section rows, seven category cells spanning 2 to 4 rows
A table split across a page breakTable 1 runs from page 2 to page 3, and the header row repeats
A footnote whose definition is pages away13 references in table cells on pages 2 and 3, all 10 definitions on page 4
A paragraph split across a page breakSection 2. Page 1 ends "...That record forms", page 2 begins "part of the approval file..."
Repeated headers and page numbersA running header and a page number on all 5 pages
A flowchartFigure 1 on page 5. None of its labels appear in the text layer, so they exist only as pixels

Step 1Parsing, with MinerU

How this was done. MinerU 3.4.4, pipeline backend, text-extraction mode, on CPU. One command, no GPU and no API key:
mineru -p test-document.pdf -o out -m txt -b pipeline -d cpu
It writes content_list.json, a flat list of typed items in reading order, which is what every later stage reads.
5pages
1table with content
1figure
15headers and page numbers, typed separately

What MinerU detected

Its layout overlay shows every region it found and how it typed each one. Click any page to enlarge it.

The merged cells survived, and the two halves became one table

The two printed halves came back as a single table. Shaded full-width rows carry colspan="4", and shaded left-hand cells carry a rowspan of between 2 and 4, so the merged cells survived. The row beginning "Recyclables collection point" was printed on page 3.

MinerU also reported a second table object on page 3, where the header row repeats. It came back with no content at all and is dropped, which is why the count above says one.

What step 1 produces

The parse, rendered to Markdown. This is the document as RAGFlow would receive it with no linking applied, and it is what the comparison later on this page uses as its baseline. Section 4 holds the ten conditions, four sections away from the table that cites them.

Output of step 110,815 characters
# Technical Circular 04/26 Schedule of Exempted Floor Areas and Conditions of Grant Issued 3 February 2026

## 1. Purpose

This circular sets out the categories of floor area that may be excluded from the calculation of gross floor area on a submission, the basis on which each exclusion is measured, and the conditions attached to each grant. It replaces Technical Circular 11/22 in full.

## 2. Basis of assessment

A claim for exclusion shall be made on the area schedule accompanying the general building plans, and shall identify each feature by the category and item number used in Table 1. A claim made after the plans have been approved shall be treated as an amendment and shall attract a fresh assessment fee. The applicant shall mark on the submitted plans the extent of every feature for which an exclusion is claimed, using a distinct hatching for each category, and shall provide a summary sheet reconciling the hatched areas against the figures entered on the area schedule. Where the development is to be constructed in phases, the schedule shall state the phase in which each feature falls, and the limits in Table 1 shall be applied to the development as a whole rather than to the individual phase. Discrepancies between the plans and the schedule shall be resolved in favour of the smaller area.

An exclusion is assessed on the area enclosed by the finished internal faces ofthe enclosing walls, measured at each floor level at which the feature occurs. Where a feature occupies more than one floor level, the area at each level is counted separately, and the aggregate is compared against the limit stated in Table 1 for that category. Where a feature is bounded on one or more sides by a structural column rather than a wall, the measurement is taken to the outer face of the column, except where the column is shared with an adjoining feature that is itself the subject of a separate claim, in which case the centre line of the shared column is used. An exclusion granted under one category may not be claimed a second time under another category, and where a feature could reasonably fall within two categories the assessing officer shall apply the category carrying the lower limit. The aggregate of all exclusions granted under Part B of Table 1 shall not in any event exceed ten per cent of the total gross floor area of the development, and the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with that aggregate cap on the area schedule submitted with the application. Where the applicant has previously obtained an exclusion for the same feature under a lapsed approval, the earlier grant confers no entitlement, and the claim shall be assessed afresh against the limits current at the date of the later submission. An assessing officer may require a site inspection before an exclusion under Part B is confirmed, and may withdraw a grant where the feature as constructed departs from the approved area schedule by more than five per cent. The measurement conventions in this section apply equally to a feature that is partly enclosed and partly open, and in such a case the area is taken to the line of the enclosing structure on the enclosed side and to the outermost edge of the roof or canopy on the open side. Where a canopy oversails a boundary, the area beyond the boundary is disregarded. The assessing officer shall record the basis of measurement adopted for each feature in the assessment record, and shall state in writing the reason for adopting the centre line convention wherever it has been applied. That record forms part of the approval file and shall be produced on request when a subsequent amendment is assessed, so that the conventions applied to a development remain consistent throughout its approval history.

## 4. Notes

Note (1) : The exclusion applies only where the chamber is provided at ground level and is accessible directly from a service lane or an off-street loading area.

Note (2) : The exclusion includes the lift machine room, the lift overrun and the associated ventilation plenum, but excludes any part of the enclosure that is used for storage or that houses equipment unrelated to the lift installation.

Note (3) : A pipe duct qualifies where it serves rainwater drainage, soil and waste disposal, or forms part of the distribution network of a mandatory plant room. A duct serving a single tenanted unit does not qualify.

Note (4) : The plant rooms exempted under this item are the hot water boiler room, the filtration plant room serving a swimming pool, and the satellite master antenna television room.

Note (5) : The exclusion is granted only where the harvested or recycled water is reticulated to at least two separate end uses within the development, and where the battery room is separated from occupied accommodation by a fire barrier of not less than two hours.

Note (6) : The sky garden shall be open to the sky over at least half its area and shall be accessible to all residents without charge. A walkway qualifies only where it is the sole means of access to the garden.

Note (7) : High headroom and void includes the void in front of a cinema screen, a theatre balcony, a banking hall, a shopping arcade, an auditorium and a sports hall.

Note (8) : Where the headroom exceeds 4.5 m only over part of the bay, the exclusion is limited to that part, measured on plan.

Note (9) : The smoke lobby qualifies only where it is provided in accordance with the code of practice for fire safety and is not used for any other purpose. A lobby that also serves a passenger lift does not qualify.

Note (10) : The exclusion applies only where the room is handed over to the utility undertaking or to the management body on completion, and where no part of it is let for commercial storage.

Step 2Linking the footnotes

This is the only stage RAGFlow does not do out of the box. A short script reads the parsed output, finds every footnote reference sitting at the end of a table cell, matches it to its definition, and writes the definition into the table that cites it.

How this was done. A Python script over content_list.json. It scans each <td> for a trailing (n) to find references, matches each number to a text item beginning Note (n) to find definitions, then appends the definition to that table as a <p class="footnote"> and deletes the standalone copy. No model and no API call: the rules are fixed, so the same input always gives the same output.

0unresolved

References outnumber definitions because notes (5), (8) and (10) are each cited from two different rows.

What changes, for one footnote

Before

Table cell on page 2:
Plant room for environmentally friendly building services (4)

The definition sits alone on page 4, 2 pages away. A chunker splitting by size or by heading has no reason to keep the two together.

After

The definition is written inside the table object that cites it:

(4) The plant rooms exempted under this item are the hot water boiler room, the filtration plant room serving a swimming pool, and the satellite master antenna television room.

The chunk is self-contained, so retrieval cannot return the row without its condition.

The two functions that do it

def find_references(items: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Every (number, item-index) where a table cell cites a footnote."""
    refs = []
    for idx, it in enumerate(items):
        if it.get("type") != "table":
            continue
        for cell in re.findall(r"<td[^>]*>(.*?)</td>", it.get("table_body", ""), re.S):
            m = CELL_REF_RE.search(_strip(cell).strip())
            if m:
                refs.append({"number": int(m.group(1)), "item": idx,
                             "page": it.get("page_idx", 0)})
    return refs


def emit(items, links, defs, seen):
    """Append each table's resolved notes to its HTML; drop standalone defs."""
    notes_for = {}
    for ln in links:
        notes_for.setdefault(ln["ref_item"], []).append((ln["number"], ln["text"]))
    # uncited definitions -> attach to the nearest preceding table
    table_indices = [i for i, it in enumerate(items) if it.get("type") == "table"
                     and it.get("table_body")]
    for num, d in defs.items():
        if num in seen:
            continue
        host = max((i for i in table_indices if i <= d["item"]), default=
                   (table_indices[0] if table_indices else None))
        if host is not None:
            notes_for.setdefault(host, []).append((num, d["text"]))

    def_items = {d["item"] for d in defs.values()}
    out = []
    for idx, it in enumerate(items):
        if idx in def_items:
            continue                                   # printed with its table
        if idx in notes_for and it.get("type") == "table":
            it = dict(it)
            notes = "".join(
                f'\n<p class="footnote" data-fn="fn-{n}">({n}) {t}</p>'
                for n, t in sorted(notes_for[idx]))
            it["table_body"] = it.get("table_body", "") + notes
            it["footnote_ids"] = [f"fn-{n}" for n, _ in sorted(notes_for[idx])]
        out.append(it)
    return out

What step 2 produces

The same document with the ten conditions moved inside the table. It is identical to the step 1 output apart from where those conditions sit, so any difference measured from here on is caused by the linking and by nothing else.

<p class="footnote" data-fn="fn-2">(2) The exclusion includes the lift machine room, the lift overrun and the associated ventilation plenum, but excludes any part of the enclosure that is used for storage or that houses equipment unrelated to the lift installation.</p>

<p class="footnote" data-fn="fn-7">(7) High headroom and void includes the void in front of a cinema screen, a theatre balcony, a banking hall, a shopping arcade, an auditorium and a sports hall.</p>
<p class="footnote" data-fn="fn-8">(8) Where the headroom exceeds 4.5 m only over part of the bay, the exclusion is limited to that part, measured on plan.</p>

# Technical Circular 04/26 Schedule of Exempted Floor Areas and Conditions of Grant Issued 3 February 2026

## 1. Purpose

This circular sets out the categories of floor area that may be excluded from the calculation of gross floor area on a submission, the basis on which each exclusion is measured, and the conditions attached to each grant. It replaces Technical Circular 11/22 in full.

## 2. Basis of assessment
Chunk 2 · Section 2, both paragraphs3,337 chars
A claim for exclusion shall be made on the area schedule accompanying the general building plans, and shall identify each feature by the category and item number used in Table 1. A claim made after the plans have been approved shall be treated as an amendment and shall attract a fresh assessment fee. The applicant shall mark on the submitted plans the extent of every feature for which an exclusion is claimed, using a distinct hatching for each category, and shall provide a summary sheet reconciling the hatched areas against the figures entered on the area schedule. Where the development is to be constructed in phases, the schedule shall state the phase in which each feature falls, and the limits in Table 1 shall be applied to the development as a whole rather than to the individual phase. Discrepancies between the plans and the schedule shall be resolved in favour of the smaller area.

An exclusion is assessed on the area enclosed by the finished internal faces ofthe enclosing walls, measured at each floor level at which the feature occurs. Where a feature occupies more than one floor level, the area at each level is counted separately, and the aggregate is compared against the limit stated in Table 1 for that category. Where a feature is bounded on one or more sides by a structural column rather than a wall, the measurement is taken to the outer face of the column, except where the column is shared with an adjoining feature that is itself the subject of a separate claim, in which case the centre line of the shared column is used. An exclusion granted under one category may not be claimed a second time under another category, and where a feature could reasonably fall within two categories the assessing officer shall apply the category carrying the lower limit. The aggregate of all exclusions granted under Part B of Table 1 shall not in any event exceed ten per cent of the total gross floor area of the development, and the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with that aggregate cap on the area schedule submitted with the application. Where the applicant has previously obtained an exclusion for the same feature under a lapsed approval, the earlier grant confers no entitlement, and the claim shall be assessed afresh against the limits current at the date of the later submission. An assessing officer may require a site inspection before an exclusion under Part B is confirmed, and may withdraw a grant where the feature as constructed departs from the approved area schedule by more than five per cent. The measurement conventions in this section apply equally to a feature that is partly enclosed and partly open, and in such a case the area is taken to the line of the enclosing structure on the enclosed side and to the outermost edge of the roof or canopy on the open side. Where a canopy oversails a boundary, the area beyond the boundary is disregarded. The assessing officer shall record the basis of measurement adopted for each feature in the assessment record, and shall state in writing the reason for adopting the centre line convention wherever it has been applied. That record forms part of the approval file and shall be produced on request when a subsequent amendment is assessed, so that the conventions applied to a development remain consistent throughout its approval history.

## 4. Notes

Note (1) : The exclusion applies only where the chamber is provided at ground level and is accessible directly from a service lane or an off-street loading area.

Note (2) : The exclusion includes the lift machine room, the lift overrun and the associated ventilation plenum, but excludes any part of the enclosure that is used for storage or that houses equipment unrelated to the lift installation.

Note (3) : A pipe duct qualifies where it serves rainwater drainage, soil and waste disposal, or forms part of the distribution network of a mandatory plant room. A duct serving a single tenanted unit does not qualify.

Note (4) : The plant rooms exempted under this item are the hot water boiler room, the filtration plant room serving a swimming pool, and the satellite master antenna television room.

Note (5) : The exclusion is granted only where the harvested or recycled water is reticulated to at least two separate end uses within the development, and where the battery room is separated from occupied accommodation by a fire barrier of not less than two hours.

Note (6) : The sky garden shall be open to the sky over at least half its area and shall be accessible to all residents without charge. A walkway qualifies only where it is the sole means of access to the garden.

Note (7) : High headroom and void includes the void in front of a cinema screen, a theatre balcony, a banking hall, a shopping arcade, an auditorium and a sports hall.

Note (8) : Where the headroom exceeds 4.5 m only over part of the bay, the exclusion is limited to that part, measured on plan.

Note (9) : The smoke lobby qualifies only where it is provided in accordance with the code of practice for fire safety and is not used for any other purpose. A lobby that also serves a passenger lift does not qualify.

Note (10) : The exclusion applies only where the room is handed over to the utility undertaking or to the management body on completion, and where no part of it is let for commercial storage.

## 5. Assessment procedure

The sequence in Figure 1 shall be followed when an exclusion is claimed.

![Figure 1. Assessment sequence for a claimed exclusion.](images/dabb753162ccc18ab203b30dea98f53ee8c693436ac59458530a969acd7ace16.jpg)

*Figure 1. Assessment sequence for a claimed exclusion.*

A claim for exclusion shall be made on the area schedule accompanying the general building plans, and shall identify each feature by the category and item number used in Table 1. A claim made after the plans have been approved shall be treated as an amendment and shall attract a fresh assessment fee. The applicant shall mark on the submitted plans the extent of every feature for which an exclusion is claimed, using a distinct hatching for each category, and shall provide a summary sheet reconciling the hatched areas against the figures entered on the area schedule. Where the development is to be constructed in phases, the schedule shall state the phase in which each feature falls, and the limits in Table 1 shall be applied to the development as a whole rather than to the individual phase. Discrepancies between the plans and the schedule shall be resolved in favour of the smaller area.

An exclusion is assessed on the area enclosed by the finished internal faces ofthe enclosing walls, measured at each floor level at which the feature occurs. Where a feature occupies more than one floor level, the area at each level is counted separately, and the aggregate is compared against the limit stated in Table 1 for that category. Where a feature is bounded on one or more sides by a structural column rather than a wall, the measurement is taken to the outer face of the column, except where the column is shared with an adjoining feature that is itself the subject of a separate claim, in which case the centre line of the shared column is used. An exclusion granted under one category may not be claimed a second time under another category, and where a feature could reasonably fall within two categories the assessing officer shall apply the category carrying the lower limit. The aggregate of all exclusions granted under Part B of Table 1 shall not in any event exceed ten per cent of the total gross floor area of the development, and the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with that aggregate cap on the area schedule submitted with the application. Where the applicant has previously obtained an exclusion for the same feature under a lapsed approval, the earlier grant confers no entitlement, and the claim shall be assessed afresh against the limits current at the date of the later submission. An assessing officer may require a site inspection before an exclusion under Part B is confirmed, and may withdraw a grant where the feature as constructed departs from the approved area schedule by more than five per cent. The measurement conventions in this section apply equally to a feature that is partly enclosed and partly open, and in such a case the area is taken to the line of the enclosing structure on the enclosed side and to the outermost edge of the roof or canopy on the open side. Where a canopy oversails a boundary, the area beyond the boundary is disregarded. The assessing officer shall record the basis of measurement adopted for each feature in the assessment record, and shall state in writing the reason for adopting the centre line convention wherever it has been applied. That record forms part of the approval file and shall be produced on request when a subsequent amendment is assessed, so that the conventions applied to a development remain consistent throughout its approval history.

#4Section 2, both paragraphs
23.41 hybrid4.23 term68.15 vector
A claim for exclusion shall be made on the area schedule accompanying the general building plans, and shall identify each feature by the category and item number used in Table 1. A claim made after the plans have been approved shall be treated as an amendment and shall attract a fresh assessment fee. The applicant shall mark on the submitted plans the extent of every feature for which an exclusion is claimed, using a distinct hatching for each category, and shall provide a summary sheet reconciling the hatched areas against the figures entered on the area schedule. Where the development is to be constructed in phases, the schedule shall state the phase in which each feature falls, and the limits in Table 1 shall be applied to the development as a whole rather than to the individual phase. Discrepancies between the plans and the schedule shall be resolved in favour of the smaller area.

An exclusion is assessed on the area enclosed by the finished internal faces ofthe enclosing walls, measured at each floor level at which the feature occurs. Where a feature occupies more than one floor level, the area at each level is counted separately, and the aggregate is compared against the limit stated in Table 1 for that category. Where a feature is bounded on one or more sides by a structural column rather than a wall, the measurement is taken to the outer face of the column, except where the column is shared with an adjoining feature that is itself the subject of a separate claim, in which case the centre line of the shared column is used. An exclusion granted under one category may not be claimed a second time under another category, and where a feature could reasonably fall within two categories the assessing officer shall apply the category carrying the lower limit. The aggregate of all exclusions granted under Part B of Table 1 shall not in any event exceed ten per cent of the total gross floor area of the development, and the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with that aggregate cap on the area schedule submitted with the application. Where the applicant has previously obtained an exclusion for the same feature under a lapsed approval, the earlier grant confers no entitlement, and the claim shall be assessed afresh against the limits current at the date of the later submission. An assessing officer may require a site inspection before an exclusion under Part B is confirmed, and may withdraw a grant where the feature as constructed departs from the approved area schedule by more than five per cent. The measurement conventions in this section apply equally to a feature that is partly enclosed and partly open, and in such a case the area is taken to the line of the enclosing structure on the enclosed side and to the outermost edge of the roof or canopy on the open side. Where a canopy oversails a boundary, the area beyond the boundary is disregarded. The assessing officer shall record the basis of measurement adopted for each feature in the assessment record, and shall state in writing the reason for adopting the centre line convention wherever it has been applied. That record forms part of the approval file and shall be produced on request when a subsequent amendment is assessed, so that the conventions applied to a development remain consistent throughout its approval history.
#5Title, section 1, and the section 2 heading

# Technical Circular 04/26 Schedule of Exempted Floor Areas and Conditions of Grant Issued 3 February 2026

## 1. Purpose

This circular sets out the categories of floor area that may be excluded from the calculation of gross floor area on a submission, the basis on which each exclusion is measured, and the conditions attached to each grant. It replaces Technical Circular 11/22 in full.

## 2. Basis of assessment

What the numbers show

One chunk out of the nine returned across both tests contains the row and the condition together, and it is the top hit in the linked base. Everything else returned either the table with no conditions or the conditions with no table. The unlinked base does retrieve the text of note (4) at rank 1; what it cannot do is say which row that note qualifies. Linking changes what a single chunk is sufficient for, which matters more here than the 1.63 point gain in ranking.
The ranking was driven by the term component, not the vector. Across all nine results the vector score spans 67.53 to 74.34, a factor of 1.10. The term score spans 4.21 to 15.81, a factor of 3.76. Embedding ran and contributed, but it did not do the discriminating on this document.

Images and multimodal embedding

The figure survives parsing as an object, and RAGFlow stores and returns images as objects: an image id is written at indexing time and returned with the chunk at search time.1 What does not happen is embedding the pixels. RAGFlow sends an image to a vision model, takes the description back as text, and passes that text to the embedding model.2 The vector is built from the caption, not the image.

This holds even when the selected embedding model is itself multimodal. jina-embeddings-v4 accepts images, and RAGFlow uses it text-only. Two open issues state the position directly:

"the image pixel content is lost after parsing"
"no way to store or query a second vector (e.g. CLIP image embedding) for the same chunk"3
"the VL embedding model's multimodal capabilities are not utilized in the current RAGFlow architecture"4
This is the one part of the pipeline established from the source code and the issue tracker rather than from a run here. Both knowledge bases in this test were built from Markdown, where the image is a relative link with nothing to resolve against, so what reached the index was the caption text.

Why this has to be self-hosted

Steps 1, 3 and 4 need nothing special. MinerU is one of the PDF parser options in RAGFlow's own ingestion pipeline, alongside DeepDoc and Naive, and is described there as "Industry-leading for complex elements like mathematical formulas and intricate layouts".5 Chunking, embedding and retrieval are the built-in components.

Step 2 is the exception. The ingestion pipeline is documented as four component types, Parser, Transformer, Chunker and Indexer, each configured through UI settings and prompt text.5 There is no code component and no external call component, so a deterministic custom stage has nowhere to live on the hosted instance. The Transformer can run a custom prompt, which is prompt-level rather than code-level customisation, and the linker is deterministic code.

Running from source is a documented mode, and the documentation names exactly this audience:

"Developers who have added new features or modified existing code and wish to debug using the source code"6

That gives filesystem access, which is what the linker needs. Components are discovered rather than hand registered: the package walks its own directory with pkgutil.walk_packages, imports each module, and adds every public class it finds to the namespace.7 A new component file placed in that directory becomes available without editing a registry.

The linker has been run as a standalone script, which is what produced the results above. Registering it as a component inside a running RAGFlow instance follows from the mechanism cited here and has not been done yet.

  2. Same commit. The vector is built from a caption rather than the pixels: rag/app/picture.py lines 97 to 100, where cv_mdl.describe(img_binary.read()) produces text that is then passed to tokenize(doc, txt, ...).
  3. Issue #15761, opened 8 June 2026, open at time of access.
